title: A pressure index gave no clear added six-month Pacific volume forecast gain at 2000-2023 origins
abstract: We tested whether a trailing three-month Southern Oscillation pressure index adds six-month Pacific warm water volume forecast information beyond seasonal ocean state and east-west temperature structure. We reused fixed NOAA GODAS and CPC ERSSTv5 records. Annual fits used earlier completed targets only. At 288 monthly origins in 2000-2023, added pressure terms reduced mean squared error by 5.94%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was -18.35% to +23.25%. RMSE fell from 0.741777 to 0.719424 in units of 10^14 cubic metres. All five model checks also had intervals across zero. Thus this test gave no clear added forecast gain. It does not show that atmospheric forcing is absent. Revised products, model form, few cycles and conditional uncertainty limit inference. The result extends prior campaign tests on overlapping data. The package gives code, exact source hashes, aggregate scores, saved uncertainty draws, a figure and numerical audits. Raw and monthly derived records remain external.

display.caption: Pressure gave no clear added forecast gain. Points show MSE reduction and bars show conditional 95% three-year block limits. The right panel shows cumulative annual score differences, not a physical trend.

citations.reason: We use the published ocean baseline, source snapshots and evaluation dates. Data overlap; this is not independent confirmation.
Prior pressure test motivated the new volume-change target. We reuse its pressure snapshot, with new analysis code.
Wind structure provides a physical reason to test atmospheric information. Our SOI is not a direct wind measure.
A different pressure index and a temperature target gave forecast value. This does not imply SOI value for volume.
